title: The core area of fruit-tree cultivation: central Jordan Valley (Levant), ca. 7000 BP
version: Palynology 48(4), 2347905. Publisher record and version of record transcribed on Academia.edu.
lineage: Same lead researcher and Tel Tsaf Area C context as the 2022 study. Table 2 adds a direct olive assay and reproduces the earlier fig date. Inspected copy at https://www.academia.edu/121002056/The_core_area_of_fruit_tree_cultivation_central_Jordan_Valley_Levant_ca_7000_BP_Langgut_2024_PALYNOLOGY.

passages.note: Tel Tsaf Area C olive branch Beta-657404 yields 7160–6950 cal BP at 68.2% probability. Fig twig Beta-585311 yields 6960–6860 cal BP at the same probability and is carried over from Langgut and Garfinkel (2022).

The author interprets the olive charcoal beyond the tree's natural range as cultivation. The Carmel coast and Galilee are proposed as possible earlier areas. The summarized evidence does not identify a source orchard, a route or the people who moved the planting material.
